## Abstract
Node scripts for the app: **build helpers** (`copy-vendor` copies the engine files into `public/vendor/`, `third-party-licenses` writes `public/licenses.txt`, `export-docs` generates the public docs) and **end-to-end tests** in WebKit (Safari's engine) emulating an iPhone 13: engines, interface, editor, endgame tables, languages, Lichess games and credits.

## Scope
Development and testing scripts only; none of them ships with the app.

## Takeaways
- Desktop WebKit **is not an iPhone** (it doesn't have iOS memory limits), but it catches Safari engine incompatibilities: that's how the 304 bug was found → the author's project notes › Investigation 2 — Prototype 0.

## Facts
- `smoke-test.mjs` passed in WebKit and Chromium with sf17 and sfhce (2026-10-24).
- `ui-test.mjs` passed in WebKit/iPhone 13 (2026-10-25): full analysis in 12.7 s on the first visit, going back via the cache in 54 ms.
- `credits-test.mjs` passed **in production** 5/5 (2026-10-25).
- `games-test.mjs` (Lichess + Chess.com) passed **in production** 20/20 (2026-10-25).
- `i18n-test.mjs` waits 0.7 s before each tap on ⚙: in WebKit's iPhone emulation a tap on ⚙ less than ~0.5 s after tapping the help's title fires no click (traced 2026-10-26). It also waits for the opening book's line before reading the texts.
- `save-test.mjs` passed 18/18 (2026-10-25). Headless WebKit has `navigator.share` but no sheet to answer it: the test replaces `navigator.share` to capture the file, then disables it to test the download.
- `curl` against the Chess.com API needs a `User-Agent` header, or Cloudflare answers 403 (browsers always send one).
- `ui-test`, `editor-test`, `tablebase-test` and `credits-test` run with a **Spanish device** (`locale: 'es-ES'`) because they look for Spanish texts; `i18n-test` covers the other languages.
- `ui-test.mjs` uses a **persistent WebKit profile** in `$TMPDIR/maia-ui-test-webkit-profile` (or `UI_TEST_PROFILE`), so the models stay cached between runs. To simulate a "first visit", delete that folder. It also saves `03-settings.png` (⚙ panel open) and, since iteration 3, checks the threats *Only moves* mode (no bar) and the number of rows per engine. Since iteration 4: the default is *Only moves* (`04-threats-only-moves.png`), it checks *Bar and moves* (`05-threats-bar.png`) and leaves the profile at the default. Since 3.5: waits for `data-done="true"` on the bar blocks (complete analysis), measures the time after a move and **fails if any move in the legends has no colour**.

## Notes
**How to run the smoke test** (from `app/`):
```bash
npm run build                                     # generates dist/
npx vite preview --port 4173 --strictPort &       # serves dist/ with COOP/COEP
node scripts/smoke-test.mjs http://localhost:4173 webkit,chromium
# only one variant / one browser:
SF_VARIANTS=sfhce node scripts/smoke-test.mjs http://localhost:4173 webkit
# interface (iPhone emulation) + screenshots:
node scripts/ui-test.mjs http://localhost:4173 <screenshots-folder>
# Lichess + Chess.com games (real APIs; leave a minute between runs):
node scripts/games-test.mjs http://localhost:4173 <screenshots-folder>
# languages:
node scripts/i18n-test.mjs http://localhost:4173 <screenshots-folder>
# endgame tables:
node scripts/tablebase-test.mjs http://localhost:4173 <screenshots-folder>
# variations, marks, comments, whole-game view:
node scripts/variations-test.mjs http://localhost:4173 <screenshots-folder>
# opening book:
node scripts/book-test.mjs http://localhost:4173 <screenshots-folder>
# save the current game + download the favourites:
node scripts/save-test.mjs http://localhost:4173 <screenshots-folder>
# credits and licence texts:
node scripts/credits-test.mjs http://localhost:4173 <screenshots-folder>
# position editor (touch taps):
node scripts/editor-test.mjs http://localhost:4173 <screenshots-folder>
# against production: replace the URL with https://jquads.pages.dev
```
Unit tests (pure functions, no browser): `npm test`.
The first run downloads ~125 MB (model + NNUE). Each browser reuses its cache for the second variant.

## Decision
- Playwright instead of a manual test: reproducible, and its WebKit is the same engine as Safari.
- `licenses.txt` generated, not written by hand: the licence texts come from the files of each dependency, so they can't go stale when a version changes (2026-10-25).
